completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.iterate_primitive_eq_integral
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.4.31 (repeated integrals): applying `g ↦ (x ↦ ∫ₐˣ g)` `n + 1` times to `f` gives
`(1/n!) ∫ₐᵇ (b - x)ⁿ f(x) dx` at `b`. Stated for `f` continuous (DLMF: continuous or piecewise
continuous).

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hasDerivAt_improper_integral_of_tendstoUniformlyOn
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.5.23–1.5.24 (Leibniz's rule for infinite integrals, `d = +∞`): suppose `f` and
`∂f/∂x` are continuous on `[a, b] × [c, ∞)`, `∫_c^∞ f(x, y) dy` converges to `I(x)` for
`x ∈ [a, b]`, and `∫_c^∞ ∂f/∂x dy` converges to `J(x)` uniformly on `[a, b]` (1.5.23, stated
as uniform convergence of `∫_c^R` as `R → ∞`, which is equivalent to the uniform smallness of
the tails). The partial derivative is required to exist for interior `x` and all `y ≥ c`;
continuity of a totalized derivative alone does not assert this. Then `I' = J` on `(a, b)`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.setIntegral_normalDomain_fst
completed.doc:

`φ₁ ≤ φ₂` continuous, `∬_D f dA = ∫ₐᵇ (∫_{φ₁(x)}^{φ₂(x)} f(x, y) dy) dx`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.setIntegral_normalDomain_snd

`ψ₁ ≤ ψ₂` continuous, `∬_D f dA = ∫_c^d (∫_{ψ₁(y)}^{ψ₂(y)} f(x, y) dx) dy`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.setIntegral_normalDomain_three

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.not_exists_sqrt_branch_punctured
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.10(vi): `z = 0` is a branch point of `√z`: there is no continuous branch of `√z` in
any punctured neighbourhood of `0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.prodConvergesDLMF_norm_iff
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.10(ix): the product `∏_{n ≥ 1} (1 + aₙ)` converges absolutely (that is,
`∏ (1 + |aₙ|)` converges) iff `∑_{n ≥ 1} |aₙ|` converges.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.prod_mtest
completed.doc:

if instead `|aₙ(z)| ≤ Mₙ` for all `n` and `z ∈ D`, with `∑ Mₙ < ∞`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.tendsto_gaussian_integral_of_growth
completed.doc:

`∫ e^{-n(x-a)²} φ(x) dx` absolutely convergent for some (hence all larger) `n`; this covers
`φ(x) = O(e^{αx²})`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourier_inversion_dlmf
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.17.8 (Fourier inversion in the normalization of 1.14.1, 1.14.4):
`(2π)⁻¹ ∫ e^{-iat} (∫ φ(x) e^{itx} dx) dt = φ(a)` for `φ` integrable, continuous, with
integrable Fourier transform.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dirichletKernel_eq
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.17.20 (closed form): `(2π)⁻¹ Σ_{k=-n}^{n} e^{ikθ} = sin((n+½)θ) / (2π sin(θ/2))`
when `sin(θ/2) ≠ 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.delta_not_regular
completed.doc:
§1.16(iii): the Dirac delta distribution is singular: it is not `Λ_f` for any locally
integrable `f`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.iteratedLineDerivOp_ofFun_apply
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.16.27: the distributional derivative `D^k f` of a locally integrable function on
`ℝⁿ` acts by `⟨D^k f, φ⟩ = (-1)^{|k|} ∫ f(x) φ^{(k)}(x) dx`. Here the multi-index `k` is
given as the list `m : Fin r → ℝⁿ` of its `r = |k|` coordinate directions, `D^k` is Mathlib's
iterated directional derivative `∂^{m}` on `𝓓'` and `φ^{(k)} = ∂^{m} φ`.

completed.doc: DLMF 1.16.33: `𝓕(P(𝐃)φ)(𝐱) = P(-𝐱) 𝓕φ(𝐱)` on Schwartz space.

distribution `u`, `P₋(𝐱) = P(-𝐱)`, derivatives in the sense of distributions.

completed.doc: The tempered form of DLMF 1.16.45: `sign' = 2δ`.

completed.doc:
The one-variable case of DLMF 1.16.36 with `P(𝐃) = d/dx`, `P₋(x) = -ix`:
`𝓕(u') = (x/i) 𝓕(u)` for a tempered distribution `u` on the line.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.discr_eq_prod_roots
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.11.9: the discriminant of `f = a_n ∏ (z - z_j)` is
`D = a_n^{2n-2} ∏_{j<k} (z_j - z_k)²` (Mathlib's `Polynomial.discr`; the cases `n = 2, 3` are
Mathlib's `Polynomial.discr_of_degree_eq_two` and `Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots`). This adapter combines Tau Ceti’s
`TauCeti.discr_C_mul` and `Polynomial.discr_prod_X_sub_C`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hermiteFunction_eigen
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.18.41–1.18.42: the Hermite functions satisfy
`-φₙ'' + x² φₙ = (2n + 1) φₙ`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hermiteFunction_hilbertBasis
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.18.42–1.18.43: the Hermite functions are an orthonormal basis of `L²(ℝ)`; hence
`f = Σₙ (∫ φₙ(y) f(y) dy) φₙ` in `L²` for `f ∈ L²(ℝ)` (1.18.43, convergence as in §1.18(ii)).

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.differentiableOn_poissonCauchyIntegral
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.15(v), after 1.15.39: for real absolutely integrable `f`, `Φ` (1.15.39) is analytic in
the upper half-plane.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fabry_transformation
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.7.19 (Fabry's transformation): if `w` solves 2.7.1 on an open set `U`, then
`W(t) = e^{f₀ t²/2} w(t²)` (that is, `w = e^{-f₀ z/2} W`, `t = z^{1/2}`) solves
`W'' + F(t) W' + G(t) W = 0` with `F(t) = 2t (f(t²) - f₀) - 1/t` and
`G(t) = 4t² (g(t²) - f₀ f(t²)/2 + f₀²/4)`, on `{t ≠ 0 : t² ∈ U}`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fabry_coefficients
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.7.ii (Fabry's transformation, the dichotomy): if `f₀² = 4g₀`, the coefficients of
the transformed equation of 2.7.19 have the expansions
`t F(t) = (2f₁ - 1) + ∑_{s≥1} 2 f_{s+1} t^{-2s}` and
`G(t) = ∑_{s≥0} 4 (g_{s+1} - f₀ f_{s+1}/2) t^{-2s}`, so its characteristic equation is
`λ² + 4(g₁ - f₀f₁/2) = 0`: either `g₁ ≠ f₀f₁/2` and the roots are unequal, or `t F(t)` and
`t² G(t)` are power series in `t⁻¹` and `t = ∞` is a regular singularity.
The variable `t` is nonzero, as in Fabry’s transformation; the totalized value at zero
does not satisfy these series identities.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.stokesC_continuous_tendsto
completed.doc: DLMF 2.11.16 (branch): `c` is continuous on `(-π, 3π)` and `c(θ) ∼ π - θ` as `θ → π`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.stokesC_re_sign
completed.doc:
DLMF §2.11(iv): `c(θ)` lies in the right half-plane for `-π < θ < π` and in the left
half-plane for `π < θ < 3π`; hence `erfc((ρ/2)^{1/2} c(θ))` is exponentially small in the first
case and exponentially close to `2` in the second.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRD_add_symEllIntRD
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.26.7: `R_D(x + λ, y + λ, z + λ) + R_D(x + μ, y + μ, z + μ)
= R_D(x, y, z) - 3/√(z (z + λ)(z + μ))`, with `λ, μ` as in (19.26.1)–(19.26.2) and `z > 0`
(`R_D`'s third argument is nonzero).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRC_addition_theta
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.26.13: `R_C(α², α² - θ) + R_C(β², β² - θ) = R_C(σ², σ² - θ)`,
`σ = (αβ + θ)/(α + β)`, where `0 < γ² - θ < γ²` for `γ = α, β, σ`, except that `σ² - θ` can be
`0`. **Corrected**: we also assume `α, β > 0` (DLMF's conditions do not fix the signs of `α, β`;
the identity fails for `α = -2, β = 3, θ = 3/2`).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRD_duplication
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.26.20: `R_D(x, y, z) = 2 R_D(x + λ, y + λ, z + λ) + 3/(√z (z + λ))`, `λ` as in
(19.26.19), under the standing assumptions with `z > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRG_duplication
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.26.21: `2 R_G(x, y, z) = 4 R_G(x + λ, y + λ, z + λ) - λ R_F(x, y, z) - √x - √y - √z`,
`λ` as in (19.26.19), under the standing assumptions.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRC_sq_eq
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.26.26: `R_C(x², y²) = R_C(a², a y)`, `a = (x + y)/2`, for
`x = 0` or `ℜ x > 0`, and `ℜ y > 0`. The first squared argument must avoid the negative
real cut; a nonzero purely imaginary `x` is outside this domain.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRG_asymp_small_x
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.27.5: `R_G(x, y, z) = R_G(0, y, z) + √x O(√(x/h))` as `x/h → 0`: for fixed
`y, z > 0`, as `x → 0+`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.wave_symEllIntR
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.18.15: `W = R_{-a}(½, ½; t + r, t - r)`, `r = √(x² + y²)`, satisfies the wave
equation `W_tt = W_xx + W_yy`, for real `t > r > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.laplace_symEllIntR
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.18.17: `U = R_{-a}(½, ½; z + iρ, z - iρ)`, `ρ = √(x² + y²)`, satisfies Laplace's
equation `U_xx + U_yy + U_zz = 0`, for real `x, y, z` with `ρ > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRJ_zero_bounds
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.24.4: `(2/√p) (2yz + yp + zp)^{-1/2} ≤ (4/(3π)) R_J(0, y, z, p) ≤ (y z p²)^{-3/8}`
for `y, z, p > 0`; the case `p = z` gives bounds for `R_D(0, y, z)` (19.24.i.p2).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.ellipsePerimeter_eq_symEllIntRG
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.24.7: the perimeter of an ellipse with semiaxes `a, b`,
`L(a, b) = 8 R_G(0, a², b²)`, with `L` the arc-length integral `ellipsePerimeter` of §19.9(i)
(`DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.ellipsePerimeter`). Valid for all real `a, b` (both sides depend on
`a², b²` only).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntR_two_eq_integral_trig
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.23.8 (`n = 2`): `R_{-a}(b₁, b₂; z₁, z₂) = 2/B(b₁, b₂) ∫₀^{π/2}
(z₁ cos² θ + z₂ sin² θ)^{-a} (cos θ)^{2b₁-1} (sin θ)^{2b₂-1} dθ`, for `b₁, b₂ > 0`,
`ℜ z₁, ℜ z₂ > 0`. The exponent `a` is any complex number (`R_{-a}` is Carlson's continuation in
`a`; both sides are entire in `a`).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRD_zero_eq_integral_trig
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.23.3: `R_D(0, y, z) = 3 ∫₀^{π/2} (y cos² θ + z sin² θ)^{-3/2} sin² θ dθ`, for
`ℜ y > 0`, `ℜ z > 0` (19.23.p1).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.integral_Ioi_symEllIntRD
completed.doc: DLMF 19.28.5: `∫_z^∞ R_D(x, y, t) dt = 6 R_F(x, y, z)` for `x, y, z > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.integral_symEllIntRD_interp
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.28.6: `∫₀¹ R_D(x, y, v² z + (1 - v²) p) dv = R_J(x, y, z, p)` for
`x, y, z, p > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntPm_inverse_sub_real
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.22.23 (second equation), real case `x ≥ y > 0`, `z ≥ x`:
`x - y = (2/a) √((a² - z₊²)(a² - z₋²))`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntR_two_eq_ordinaryHypergeometric
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.25.43: `R_{-a}(b₁, b₂; z₁, z₂) = z₂^{-a} ₂F₁(a, b₁; b₁ + b₂; 1 - z₁/z₂)`, for
`z₁, z₂ ∈ ℂ \ (-∞, 0]` with `|1 - z₁/z₂| < 1` and `arg z₁ - arg z₂ ∈ (-π, π)` (so that
`z₂^{-a}` and the homogeneity of `R` match the principal branches), `b₁ + b₂ ∉ {0, -1, …}`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRF_lemniscatic
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.20.3 (general lemniscatic case), **domain-restricted** to real `x, y > 0`:
`R_F(x, a, y) = R_{-1/4}(3/4, 1/2; a², xy)`, `a = (x + y)/2`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRF_lemniscatic_complex
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.20.3, corrected complex form: `R_F(x, a, y) = R_{-1 / 4}(3 / 4, 1/2; a², xy)`, `a = (x + y)/2`, for complex
`x, y` with `ℜ x > 0` and `ℜ y > 0`. **Corrected from the printed DLMF formula**: DLMF states it
under the 19.16(i) constraints only, but it fails there, e.g. at `x = -1 + i`, `y = -1 + 2i` the
two sides differ by a factor `±i` (independent mpmath check, 2026-10-25).

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRD_lemniscatic
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.20.23 (general lemniscatic case), **domain-restricted** to real `x, y > 0`:
`R_D(x, y, a) = R_{-3/4}(5/4, 1/2; a², xy)`, `a = (x + y)/2`.

completed.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRD_lemniscatic_complex
completed.doc:
DLMF 19.20.23, corrected complex form: `R_D(x, y, a) = R_{-3 / 4}(5 / 4, 1/2; a², xy)`, `a = (x + y)/2`, for complex
`x, y` with `ℜ x > 0` and `ℜ y > 0`. **Corrected from the printed DLMF formula**: DLMF states it
under the 19.16(i) constraints only, but it fails there, e.g. at `x = -1 + i`, `y = -1 + 2i` the
two sides differ by a factor `±i` (independent mpmath check, 2026-10-25).

completed.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.genHG_3F2_unit_recurrence_two

completed.doc:
DLMF 35.2 (paragraph after 35.2.1): if `|f(X)| < etr(-X₀X)` on `Ω` for some `X₀ ∈ Ω`, the
Laplace transform 35.2.1 converges absolutely for every complex symmetric `𝐙` with

Identity under the stated parameter and domain assumptions: `∫ x : ℝ in Set.Ioi 0, qLaguerre α

completed.doc: The `1φ1` summation `1φ1(a;c;q,c/a) = (c/a;q)_∞/(c;q)_∞` (DLMF 17.5.E5).

As `q → 1⁻`, the Jackson integral of a continuous function tends to its Riemann integral (DLMF
17.2.E47).

completed.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelCapital_terminates
completed.doc:
DLMF 11.9.9: when `μ + ν` or `μ - ν` is a positive odd integer, the capital Lommel
function is its finite inverse-power expansion, including removable exceptional parameters.

completed.name: DLMF.Struve.struveH_relative_bound
completed.doc:
DLMF 11.4.14–11.4.15, with the exponential subtraction corrected: the relative error of
`H_ν(z)` is bounded by `(2/3) * (exp (‖z‖² / (4d)) - 1)`. Any positive lower bound `d` for

completed.name: DLMF.Zeta.hasSum_multiple_sum_riemannZeta
completed.doc:
DLMF 25.6.5: for `k ≥ 1`,
`ζ(k+1) = (1/k!) ∑_{n₁,…,n_k ≥ 1} 1/(n₁⋯n_k (n₁ + ⋯ + n_k))`, stated as the (absolutely
convergent) sum of the `k`-fold series being `k! ζ(k+1)`; the summation variables are

completed.name: DLMF.Zeta.iteratedDeriv_two_riemannZeta_zero

DLMF 25.6.12: `ζ''(0) = -½ (ln 2π)² + ½ γ² - π²/24 + γ₁`, with the Stieltjes constant `γ₁`
of 25.2.5.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hasDerivAt_integral_fixed_limits
newDeclarations.doc:
A continuous partial derivative on a compact rectangle may be integrated under the
integral sign. The derivative is assumed to exist for interior parameter values.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.isCompact_normalDomain_fst
newDeclarations.doc: A planar region between two continuous graphs over a compact interval is compact.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.polyOp_apply_eigenfunctional
newDeclarations.doc:
A linear functional on which each operator acts by a scalar evaluates the polynomial in
those operators by substituting the same scalars.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dlmfFourierSchwartz_lineDeriv
newDeclarations.doc:
The DLMF Fourier transform sends a directional derivative to multiplication by
`-I * inner x v`. This specializes Mathlib’s `SchwartzMap.fourierInv_lineDerivOp_eq`.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dlmfFourierSchwartz_dlmfD
newDeclarations.doc: The DLMF differential operator `D_j = (1 / I) ∂_j` transforms to multiplication by `-x_j`.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.polyEval_hasTemperateGrowth
newDeclarations.doc: A complex polynomial in the real coordinate functions has temperate growth.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.polyOp_intertwine
newDeclarations.doc:
A linear map intertwining two families of operators also intertwines every polynomial
in those families, preserving the fixed order in `polyOp`.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.lineDeriv_dlmfFourierSchwartz
newDeclarations.doc:
A directional derivative of the DLMF Fourier transform corresponds to multiplying the
original Schwartz function by `I * inner x v`, including DLMF’s frequency normalization.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.polyOp_pairing
newDeclarations.doc:
A bilinear pairing transposes a polynomial in operators to the corresponding polynomial
in their adjoints, provided the latter commute.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.schwartz_lineDeriv_comm
newDeclarations.doc:
Directional derivatives of smooth Schwartz functions commute. The proof adapts
Tau Ceti’s `TestFunction.lineDerivOp_comm`, using Mathlib’s symmetric second derivative.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dlmfD_commute
newDeclarations.doc: The coordinate differential operators `D_i` and `D_j` commute on Schwartz space.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.temperedPolyDiffOp_apply
newDeclarations.doc:
Applying a polynomial differential operator to a tempered distribution transfers the
operators to the test function with a minus sign on each coordinate derivative.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.coordinate_hasTemperateGrowth
newDeclarations.doc: A real coordinate function, viewed as complex valued, has temperate growth.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.polyOp_coordinateMul_apply
newDeclarations.doc:
A polynomial in coordinate multiplication operators acts pointwise as the corresponding
polynomial function, with a common complex scale factor on the coordinates.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dlmfD_dlmfFourierSchwartz
newDeclarations.doc:
The DLMF operator `D_j` applied to a Fourier transform is the transform of multiplication
by the original coordinate `x_j`.

newDeclarations.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.dlmfFourierSchwartz_deriv
newDeclarations.doc:
In DLMF's normalization, differentiating a Schwartz Fourier transform corresponds to

counterexamples.source:
/-
Independent counterexample to parameter analyticity propagated from an initial point across a
disconnected spatial domain. This file imports definitions only, not the admitted theorem.
-/
import DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.ODE.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.RealDeriv

open Complex Filter Set
open scoped Topology

namespace ODEParameterCounterexample

/-- The two open half-planes, without their common boundary. -/
def domain : Set ℂ := {z | z.re ≠ 0}

/-- Constant in the spatial variable on each component, with a conjugate parameter on the right. -/
noncomputable def solution (u z : ℂ) : ℂ := if z.re < 0 then 0 else star u

/-- The spatial domain is open. -/
lemma domain_isOpen : IsOpen domain := isOpen_ne.preimage continuous_re

/-- Every spatial germ of the solution family is constant. -/
lemma solution_locally_constant (u z : ℂ) (hz : z ∈ domain) :
    solution u =ᶠ[𝓝 z] fun _ => solution u z := by
  by_cases hn : z.re < 0
  · filter_upwards [(isOpen_lt continuous_re continuous_const).mem_nhds hn] with y hy
    simp [solution, hn, hy]
  · have hp : 0 < z.re := lt_of_le_of_ne (not_lt.mp hn) (Ne.symm hz)
    filter_upwards [(isOpen_lt continuous_const continuous_re).mem_nhds hp] with y hy
    simp [solution, hn, not_lt.mpr hy.le]

/-- All spatial first derivatives vanish. -/
lemma solution_deriv_zero (u z : ℂ) (hz : z ∈ domain) : deriv (solution u) z = 0 := by
  exact ((hasDerivAt_const z (solution u z)).congr_of_eventuallyEq
    (solution_locally_constant u z hz)).deriv

/-- The family solves the zero-coefficient homogeneous second-order equation on the domain. -/
lemma solution_solves (u : ℂ) :
    DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.IsLinODE2SolOn 0 0 0 (solution u) domain := by
  intro z hz
  refine ⟨((hasDerivAt_const z (solution u z)).congr_of_eventuallyEq
    (solution_locally_constant u z hz)).differentiableAt, ?_⟩
  have hd : deriv (solution u) =ᶠ[𝓝 z] fun _ => 0 := by
    filter_upwards [domain_isOpen.mem_nhds hz] with y hy using solution_deriv_zero u y hy
  simpa using (hasDerivAt_const z (0 : ℂ)).congr_of_eventuallyEq hd

/-- Conjugation has no complex derivative at zero, since its real derivative sends `1` to `1`
but `I` to `-I`. -/
lemma conjugation_not_differentiable : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℂ (star : ℂ → ℂ) 0 := by
  intro h
  have hr := h.hasDerivAt.complexToReal_fderiv.unique Complex.conjCLE.hasFDerivAt
  have h1 := congrArg (fun L : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ => L 1) hr
  have hI := congrArg (fun L : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ => L I) hr
  simp only [smul_apply, one_apply_eq_self, smul_eq_mul,
    mul_one, Complex.conjCLE_apply, map_one] at h1
  rw [h1] at hI
  have him := congrArg Complex.im hI
  norm_num at him

/-- All the old spatial and initial-data assumptions hold, while parameter holomorphy fails on
the second spatial component. The coefficient maps are the constant zero maps. -/
theorem counterexample :
    IsOpen domain ∧ (-1 : ℂ) ∈ domain ∧ (1 : ℂ) ∈ domain ∧
      (∀ u, DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.IsLinODE2SolOn 0 0 0 (solution u) domain) ∧
      Differentiable ℂ (fun u => solution u (-1)) ∧
      Differentiable ℂ (fun u => deriv (solution u) (-1)) ∧
      ¬ DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun u => solution u 1) univ := by
  refine ⟨domain_isOpen, by norm_num [domain], by norm_num [domain], solution_solves,
    ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa [solution] using (differentiable_const (0 : ℂ))
  · have h : (fun u => deriv (solution u) (-1)) = fun _ : ℂ => 0 :=
      funext fun u => solution_deriv_zero u (-1) (by norm_num [domain])
    rw [h]
    exact differentiable_const _
  · intro h
    apply conjugation_not_differentiable
    have hh := (differentiableOn_univ.mp h) 0
    norm_num [solution] at hh
    exact hh

end ODEParameterCounterexample

counterexamples.source:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.InfiniteSum.NatInt

/-!
# The excluded zero argument in Fabry's coefficient identities

This independent example uses zero functions and zero coefficient sequences, with exterior
radius -1. The old hypotheses allowed t=0, where the first claimed sum is -1 rather than 0.
The admitted Fabry coefficient theorem is neither imported nor invoked.
-/


open Complex

/-- Zero coefficients satisfy the exterior expansions at radius -1, but at t=0 the
first Fabry identity would assert that a series of sum -1 has sum zero. -/
theorem fabry_coefficients_zero_counterexample :
    (∀ z : ℂ, (-1 : ℝ) < ‖z‖ → HasSum (fun s : ℕ => (0 : ℂ) * z⁻¹ ^ s) 0) ∧
      (0 : ℂ) ^ 2 = 4 * 0 ∧
      (-1 : ℝ) < ‖(0 : ℂ) ^ 2‖ ∧
      ¬HasSum (fun s : ℕ =>
        (if s = 0 then 2 * (0 : ℂ) - 1 else 2 * 0) * ((0 : ℂ)⁻¹ ^ 2) ^ s)
        ((0 : ℂ) * (2 * 0 * (0 - 0) - 1 / 0)) := by
  refine ⟨fun z hz => by simp, by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  intro h
  have hm : HasSum (fun s : ℕ =>
      (if s = 0 then 2 * (0 : ℂ) - 1 else 2 * 0) * ((0 : ℂ)⁻¹ ^ 2) ^ s) (-1) := by
    convert! hasSum_ite_eq (0 : ℕ) (-1 : ℂ) using 1
    ext s
    by_cases hs : s = 0 <;> simp [hs]
  have he := hm.unique h
  norm_num at he

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regenerate the declaration links and statuses of the DLMF acquisition ledgers.

Usage (from the project root, after `lake build` and scripts/DumpDLMF.lean):

    python3 scripts/dlmf_ledgers.py dlmf-tags.json [--dry] LEDGER.md ...

The tag dump written by scripts/DumpDLMF.lean is the source of truth for every declaration
carrying an `@[dlmf]` attribute: its location and its status from the compiled axiom audit.
Linked declarations without a DLMF tag fall back to a source scan (location, and an explicit
`sorry` in the declaration body for the status). For each ledger the script

* rewrites every link `[name](file.lean#Ln) (status)` to the current file and line, and the
  status to `proved`, `admitted`, or `proved from admissions` (a proof without `sorry` of its
  own that depends on admitted lemmas; known only for tagged declarations), keeping the
  `definition`/`defined` labels;
* appends to each equation line `- [ID](https://dlmf.nist.gov/ID): ...` the project
  declarations tagged `ID` that the line does not yet mention, and Mathlib or TauCeti
  declarations tagged `ID` as upstream pointers;
* inserts a line for each tagged ID of the ledger's chapters that has no line yet, after the
  last line of the same section;
* rewrites the module admission counts (`- [Mod](DLMF/...lean): N admissions.` and the
  `N definitions, M statements, P proved, A admitted.` inventory lines);
* reports links whose declaration is missing, and links whose declaration carries DLMF tags
  none of which is the line's ID.
Prose is never changed.
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import sys

DECL = re.compile(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial)\s+)*'
                  r'(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|instance|structure|inductive|class)\s+([^\s(:{\[]+)', re.M)
LINK = re.compile(r'\[(`?)([^\]`]+)`?\]\(([^)#]*\.lean)(?:#L(\d+))?\) '
                  r'\((admitted|proved|proved from admissions|definition|defined|nonstandard axioms)\)')
EQLINE = re.compile(r'^- \[(\d+\.\d+(?:\.(?:[ETF]\d+(?:_\d+)*|[ivx]+))?)\]\(https://dlmf\.nist\.gov/\1\):')


def strip_comments(s):
    s = re.sub(r'/-.*?-/', lambda m: '\n' * m.group(0).count('\n'), s, flags=re.S)
    return re.sub(r'--[^\n]*', '', s)


def scan_source(roots):
    """Declarations by written and qualified names, with locations and admission flags."""
    idx = collections.defaultdict(list)
    admitted = collections.Counter()
    stats = {}
    for root in roots:
        for dp, _, fs in os.walk(root):
            for f in fs:
                if not f.endswith('.lean'):
                    continue
                p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dp, f))
                s = strip_comments(open(p).read())
                ms = list(DECL.finditer(s))
                scopes = iter(re.finditer(
                    r'^(?:@\[[^\n]*\][ \t]*)?(?:(?:public|noncomputable)[ \t]+)*'
                    r'(namespace[ \t]+(\S+)|section(?:[ \t]+\S+)?|end(?:[ \t]+\S+)?)[ \t]*$',
                    s, re.M))
                scope = next(scopes, None)
                namespace = ''
                parents = []
                nd = nt = 0
                for i, m in enumerate(ms):
                    while scope is not None and scope.start() < m.start():
                        command, opened = scope.group(1), scope.group(2)
                        if command.startswith('namespace '):
                            parents.append(namespace)
                            namespace = (opened.removeprefix('_root_.')
                                         if opened.startswith('_root_.') else
                                         '.'.join(filter(None, [namespace, opened])))
                        elif command.startswith('section'):
                            parents.append(namespace)

                            namespace = parents.pop()

                                 else '.'.join(filter(None, [namespace, name])))

def theorem_status(e):
    """Ledger label for the status of a dumped theorem."""
    if e['status'] == 'admitted' and e.get('sorryDirect') is False:
        return 'proved from admissions'
    return {'nonstandard': 'nonstandard axioms'}.get(e['status'], e['status'])


def suffixes(name):
    parts = name.split('.')
    return ['.'.join(parts[i:]) for i in range(len(parts))]


def main():
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != '--dry']
    dry = '--dry' in sys.argv
    dump = json.load(open(args[0]))
    ledgers = args[1:]
    entries = dump['entries']
    by_decl = collections.defaultdict(list)
    by_suffix = collections.defaultdict(list)
    by_id = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for e in entries:
        by_decl[e['decl']].append(e)
        for s in suffixes(e['decl']):
            by_suffix[s].append(e)
        by_id[e['dlmf']].append(e)
    src, admitted, stats = scan_source(['DLMF', 'DLMFMathlib'])

    def resolve(name, path):
        """Dump entry or source record for a linked name, preferring the linked file."""
        # An untagged declaration's exact name takes precedence over another declaration's
        # tagged suffix: e.g. Statistical.incBeta is distinct from Statistical.Real.incBeta.
        if name.startswith(('DLMF.', 'DLMFMathlib.')) and name not in by_decl:
            recs = src.get(name, [])
            hit = [r for r in recs if r[0] == path] or recs
            if len(hit) == 1:
                return 'src', hit[0]
        for key in suffixes(name):
            cands = by_decl.get(key) or by_suffix.get(key) or []
            cands = list({c['decl']: c for c in cands}.values())
            if cands:
                hit = [c for c in cands if os.path.normpath(c['file']) == path] or cands
                if len(hit) == 1 or len({c['file'] for c in hit}) == 1:
                    return 'dump', hit[0]
            recs = src.get(key)
            if recs:
                hit = [r for r in recs if r[0] == path] or recs
                return 'src', hit[0]
        return None, None

    for ledger in ledgers:
        base = os.path.dirname(ledger)
        rel = lambda p: os.path.relpath(p, base or '.')
        text = open(ledger).read()
        full_names = '`DLMF.' in text
        chapters = {m.split('.')[0] for m in re.findall(r'^- \[(\d+\.\d+\.[^\]]+)\]', text, re.M)}
        stat = collections.Counter()
        report = []

        def label(name):
            if full_names:
                return f'`{name}`'
            parts = name.split('.')
            return '.'.join(parts[2:]) if parts[0] == 'DLMF' and len(parts) > 2 else name

        def deflabel():
            return 'defined' if '(defined)' in text else 'definition'

        def fmt(e):
            st = theorem_status(e) if e['kind'] == 'theorem' else deflabel()
            return f"[{label(e['decl'])}]({rel(e['file'])}#L{e['line']}) ({st})"

        def relink(m, line_id=None):
            bt, name, path, _, status = m.groups()
            path_n = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, path))
            kind, rec = resolve(name, path_n)
            if kind is None:
                stat['missing'] += 1
                report.append(f'missing declaration: {name} ({path})')
                return m.group(0), None
            if kind == 'dump':
                file, line, decl = os.path.normpath(rec['file']), rec['line'], rec['decl']
                new = status if status in ('definition', 'defined') else theorem_status(rec)
                stat['from dump'] += 1
                if line_id and line_id not in {e['dlmf'] for e in by_decl[decl]}:
                    report.append(f'{line_id}: {decl} is tagged '
                                  f'{sorted({e["dlmf"] for e in by_decl[decl]})}')
            else:
                file, line, k, sor = rec
                decl = name
                new = status if status in ('definition', 'defined') else ('admitted' if sor else 'proved')
                stat['from source'] += 1
            if new != status:
                stat[f'{status} -> {new}'] += 1
            if os.path.normpath(file) != path_n:
                stat['moved'] += 1
            return f'[{bt}{name}{bt}]({rel(file)}#L{line}) ({new})', decl

        out = []
        seen_ids = set()
        # Lines sharing an ID: what any of them mentions counts for all, and missing
        # declarations are appended to the last of them only.
        lines_in = text.split('\n')
        id_text = collections.defaultdict(str)
        last_line = {}
        for k, l in enumerate(lines_in):
            em0 = EQLINE.match(l)
            if em0:
                id_text[em0.group(1)] += l + '\n'
                last_line[em0.group(1)] = k
        for k, line in enumerate(lines_in):
            em = EQLINE.match(line)
            if not em:
                out.append(LINK.sub(lambda m: relink(m)[0], line))
                continue
            lid = em.group(1)
            seen_ids.add(lid)
            linked = set()

            def rep(m):
                s, decl = relink(m, lid)
                if decl:
                    linked.add(decl)
                return s
            line = LINK.sub(rep, line)
            if last_line[lid] != k:
                out.append(line)
                continue
            all_text = id_text[lid]
            for m in LINK.finditer(all_text):
                linked.add(m.group(2))
            linked_suffix = {s for d in linked for s in suffixes(d)}
            extra = []
            for e in by_id.get(lid, []):
                if (e['decl'] in linked or e['decl'] in linked_suffix
                        or label(e['decl']).strip('`') in all_text):
                    continue
                if e['project'] == 'lean-DLMF':
                    extra.append(fmt(e))
                    stat['appended'] += 1
                elif e['docUrl'] or e['sourceUrl']:
                    if e['decl'] in all_text:
                        continue
                    extra.append(f"{e['project']}: [`{e['decl']}`]({e['docUrl'] or e['sourceUrl']})")
                    stat['upstream pointers'] += 1
            if extra:
                body = line[:-1] if line.endswith('.') else line
                line = body + '; ' + '; '.join(extra) + '.'
            out.append(line)

        # Tagged IDs of this ledger's chapters that have no line yet.
        missing_ids = sorted({i for i in by_id if i.split('.')[0] in chapters and i not in seen_ids
                              and any(e['project'] == 'lean-DLMF' for e in by_id[i])},
                             key=lambda i: [int(x) if x.isdigit() else x
                                            for x in re.split(r'[.ETF]', i) if x])
        for lid in missing_ids:
            sec = '.'.join(lid.split('.')[:2]) + '.'
            pos = max((k for k, l in enumerate(out) if l.startswith(f'- [{sec}')), default=None)
            if pos is None:
                report.append(f'no section for new ID {lid}')
                continue
            items = '; '.join(fmt(e) for e in by_id[lid] if e['project'] == 'lean-DLMF')
            out.insert(pos + 1, f'- [{lid}](https://dlmf.nist.gov/{lid}): {items}.')
            stat['new lines'] += 1
        text = '\n'.join(out)

        # Module counts.
        def r1(m):
            p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, m.group(2)))
            return m.group(0) if p not in stats else f'- [{m.group(1)}]({m.group(2)}): {admitted[p]} admissions.'
        text = re.sub(r'^- \[(\w+)\]\(([^)]+\.lean)\): \d+ admissions\.', r1, text, flags=re.M)

        def r2(m):
            p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, m.group(2)))
            if p not in stats:
                return m.group(0)
            d, n = stats[p]
            a = admitted[p]
            return f'- [{m.group(1)}]({m.group(2)}): {d} definitions, {n} statements, {n - a} proved, {a} admitted.'
        text = re.sub(r'^- \[([^\]]+\.lean)\]\(([^)]+\.lean)\): \d+ definitions, \d+ statements, '
                      r'\d+ proved, \d+ admitted\.', r2, text, flags=re.M)

        print(f'{ledger}: {dict(stat)}')
        for r in report:
            print('  ' + r)
        if not dry:
            open(ledger, 'w').write(text)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
